title: Apprenticeships — earn and learn
weekly_outcome: Students understand the basic features of an apprenticeship.
weekly_outcome_verbatim: Students understand the basic features of an apprenticeship.
objective: I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.
objective_verbatim: I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.
display_objective: I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 3, 18–22 January 2027. Tuesday 19 January 2027, P3. One 40-minute formative lesson for up to five learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks; Week 6 assessing. Source Week 5 retains its mixed evidence role. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: Exact E18 weekly outcome, F18 focus, G18 lesson outcome and J18 evidence retained. H18 sequence and I18 timing retained. Prepared invented profiles replace real vacancies and websites. Learners label pay, training, employer and entry needs, check myths and connect a chosen profile to its sector. Review is private. K18 reduced choices, visual model, sentence starts and usual access retained. Aspire is optional. All example entry and application details are practice information, not universal requirements or real eligibility judgements.

source_sequence_verbatim: Arrival/retrieval linked to previous careers learning → I Do: explain/model apprenticeships — earn and learn with concrete examples → We Do: guided sorting/annotating/scenario discussion → You Do: Use an accessible apprenticeship profile/vacancy; label pay, training, employer and entry requirements; myth/fact check; connect to chosen sector. → 1:1/whole-class review → exit check and add evidence to Careers Portfolio.
timing: Recall learn and earn from Week 2 with picture choices.
Pre-teach words; explain paid work plus training and model profile A.
Label profile A; compare entry needs and check a myth and hinge privately.
Choose B or C; make an apprenticeship fact card with pay, training, employer, entry need and one application need.
Check earn and learn plus an application need; one NS and reply; bank fact card in Careers Portfolio.

routes.Supported: Read one profile field at a time. Keep the pictures, model, word bank and sentence starts. Offer two labels or two details to choose from. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Log supplied labels and modelled answers.
routes.Independent: Choose B or C. Label pay, training, employer and entry need; explain paid work plus training and identify one thing needed to apply. Keep normal reading and communication aids.
routes.Aspire: Compare the chosen profile with A. Explain why entry needs may differ and give one question to check before a real application. No extra writing or public presentation required.

myths.claim: An apprenticeship includes paid work and training.
myths.reason: An apprentice earns pay for work and learns through training.

myths.claim: An apprentice does paid work but has no training.
myths.reason: Training is part of an apprenticeship.

colour_blind_safe: Icons, captions, labels and words carry meaning; no colour-only codes.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, people, roles, employers and profile details are invented and generic. Pictures are symbols, not real people or places. No named employer, provider, scheme, website, place, product or platform. Entry and application needs are for the practice cards only.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal grades, family jobs or finances requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Either profile can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and allows correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.
worked_example_and_fade: After A, choose which pair describes the apprenticeship: A paid work and training; B paid work only. Key A. If unclear, point to A’s Pay and Training fields and model both. Keep icons, the full example, words and frames. Fade answer cues only; usual aids stay available.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: short labelled profile, clear icons, model and two-choice scaffolds. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, one instruction, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm predictable tasks, pass, supported pause/return; no cold calling. Sensory and Physical: large clear pictures/text, pointing instead of moving cards, no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language; explain route words before asking for them.
misconceptions: An apprenticeship is not paid work without training or a course with no paid job. An employer provides the job; a trainer helps learning. They are different roles and may work together. A practice card’s entry skill is not a rule for every apprenticeship. Applying is asking to be considered, not a promise of a place.

evidence.description: Apprenticeship fact card. Keep actual explanation, one sourced application need, labels, chosen profile and sector, access, prompts, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Apprenticeship fact card. Keep chosen profile and sector, pay, training, employer, entry need, earn-and-learn explanation, one application need, first response, actual access, answer prompts, one NS and reply. Secure explanation includes both paid work and training. Secure application-need evidence identifies an Entry need or To apply detail from the selected card. Do not substitute a pay amount or job title for a requirement. Mark the two checks separately and retain partial evidence. A pass is unobserved.
where_this_leads: This helps me understand an apprenticeship and ask what I need before I apply.

I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.
Source: BUILD Careers physical row 18 / Spring 1 row 3. E18 weekly outcome, F18 focus, G18 lesson outcome, H18 sequence, I18 timing and J18 evidence.

An apprenticeship combines paid work with training. Learners read an invented profile, label its features and identify one application need. The examples are generic trades, not real vacancies. Entry skills and application tasks are invented for this activity, not universal rules or a judgement about any learner’s eligibility.

Explain earn and learn as paid work plus training. Identify pay, training, employer and entry need on the chosen profile. Name one relevant thing needed to apply and point to its source. Record explanation and application need separately.

Books, pens, profiles, Vocabulary Mat and evidence record. Adult may cut reusable cards before teaching. All work is reading, matching and explaining; no tools, food handling or practical trade work. Confirm private help and a supported pause/return. No internet, login or phone.
This helps me understand an apprenticeship and ask what I need before I apply.
Recall learn and earn from Week 2 with picture choices.
Pre-teach words; explain paid work plus training and model profile A.
Label profile A; compare entry needs and check a myth and hinge privately.
Choose B or C; make an apprenticeship fact card with pay, training, employer, entry need and one application need.
Check earn and learn plus an application need; one NS and reply; bank fact card in Careers Portfolio.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes, following I18. Processing time and brief pauses are included. Slides 7 and 8 share the 23–35-minute task window.

0–5: recall learn and earn using pay and training pictures. Either pointing or words are valid. Supply the Week 2 idea if absent. 5–9: read the exact outcome and teach apprentice, pay, training, employer, entry need and apply. 9–13: model A. Identify pay for checking/mending bikes and planned lessons/practice. Explain both together: paid work plus training. Point to the small repair workshop as employer and reading a safety note as the practice entry need. Model an application need using the exact profile.

13–19: label A with pay, training, employer and entry need. Read one field at a time. Compare A reading a note with B measuring a length: requirements in the practice cards differ. Model finding the To apply field. 19–23: myth/fact check and private hinge. Correct no-training claims; re-model if needed and use the parallel check.

23–35: choose B woodwork or C food making, or let an adult offer a neutral choice for a made-up person. In a book, type or use usual aid/scribe to make a fact card. Record sector, pay, training, employer and entry need. Explain paid work plus training and name one thing needed to apply from Entry need or To apply. Both choices use the same checks; no learner has to say this is a future career plan.

35–38: privately check explanation and application need; give one NS and retain the reply. 38–40: say or show paid work plus training and one requirement from the chosen profile. Add the actual fact card to Careers Portfolio. No public retelling or personal qualification disclosure.

Read one profile field at a time. Keep the pictures, model, word bank and sentence starts. Offer two labels or two details to choose from. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Log supplied labels and modelled answers.
Choose B or C. Label pay, training, employer and entry need; explain paid work plus training and identify one thing needed to apply. Keep normal reading and communication aids.
Compare the chosen profile with A. Explain why entry needs may differ and give one question to check before a real application. No extra writing or public presentation required.

After A, choose which pair describes the apprenticeship: A paid work and training; B paid work only. Key A. If unclear, point to A’s Pay and Training fields and model both. Keep icons, the full example, words and frames. Fade answer cues only; usual aids stay available.

Main: an apprentice has A paid work only; B paid work and training. Key B. If unclear, read the two fields together and recheck privately. Parallel: which card fits earn and learn? A a paid job with planned lessons; B a course with no paid job. Key A. A pass is unobserved. Myth/fact keys are Fact, Myth, Myth; require a clue where possible.

Cognition and Learning: short labelled profile, clear icons, model and two-choice scaffolds. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, one instruction, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm predictable tasks, pass, supported pause/return; no cold calling. Sensory and Physical: large clear pictures/text, pointing instead of moving cards, no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language; explain route words before asking for them.

Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task. I Do: point to pay and learning icons. We Do: prompt the matching label. You Do: log help and supplied details without silently completing the fact card.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal grades, family jobs or finances requested.

Either profile can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and allows correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.

Exact source evidence: Apprenticeship fact card. Keep chosen profile and sector, pay, training, employer, entry need, earn-and-learn explanation, one application need, first response, actual access, answer prompts, one NS and reply. Secure explanation includes both paid work and training. Secure application-need evidence identifies an Entry need or To apply detail from the selected card. Do not substitute a pay amount or job title for a requirement. Mark the two checks separately and retain partial evidence. A pass is unobserved.

An apprenticeship is not paid work without training or a course with no paid job. An employer provides the job; a trainer helps learning. They are different roles and may work together. A practice card’s entry skill is not a rule for every apprenticeship. Applying is asking to be considered, not a promise of a place.

One NS may be add training to the explanation or use the Entry need field. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual banked evidence. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and a reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.

All people, roles, employers and profile details are invented. Employer types only: small bike repair workshop, wood workshop and bakery. Pictures are generic symbols, not real people or places. No named provider, scheme, website or product. No pay rates, entry grades, age rules or actual openings stated. Staff check current requirements and support through the usual advice route before any real application. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures.

H18 profile/vacancy task uses prepared invented profiles; no live research. Its labels, myth/fact check and link to a chosen sector are retained. K18 website suggestions become in-pack cards. I can explain that an apprenticeship combines paid work with training and identify one thing I would need to apply.

An apprenticeship combines paid work with training. Accept equivalent wording or aided selections that communicate both parts. Paid work alone or training alone is incomplete. No pay rates, age rules, entry grades or actual vacancies are asserted. All three profiles are invented classroom examples.

Sector bike repair. Pay: paid to help check and mend bikes. Training: planned lessons and practice with a trainer. Employer: small bike repair workshop. Entry need: read a short safety note. To apply: complete a short form about a skill to learn. One valid need is reading the safety note; completing that form also meets the application-need check. Keep source field visible.

Model check A: paid work and training. Main hinge B: paid work and training. Parallel A: paid job with planned lessons. If unclear, point to Pay and Training together, model again and recheck privately. Keep normal aids and word bank; fade only answer cues. A pass is unobserved.

1 Fact: paid work plus training. 2 Myth: training is part of an apprenticeship. 3 Myth: A asks for reading a safety note; B measuring; C following steps. Use the card details as evidence. Do not turn these made-up entry skills into universal rules.
The employer gives the job; the trainer supports learning. These are roles, not named organisations, and may work together. Learners should not use the job title as the employer answer.

Sector woodwork. Pay: paid to help measure and smooth wood. Training: planned lessons and practice with a trainer. Employer: a small wood workshop. Entry need: measure a short length with a ruler. To apply: give an example of following an instruction. Valid need: measuring with a ruler or preparing the requested example. The fact card explains paid work plus training.

Sector food making. Pay: paid to help weigh and mix food. Training: planned lessons and practice in a training kitchen. Employer: a small bakery. Entry need: follow a short list of steps. To apply: complete a short form about a skill to practise. Valid need: following the steps or completing the requested form. The fact card explains paid work plus training.

B and C meet the same success checks. Choosing a sector is a lesson choice, not a personal destination commitment. Offer a neutral choice for an invented person if preferred. Use two labels at a time: Pay/Training for paid work; Employer/Entry need for the business or skill. Record supplied details. Accept learner wording that preserves meaning.

Accept a detail from Entry need or To apply, with its source. Do not accept only a pay amount, employer type or role title as the required application need. Reading support, an aid or exact scribe are valid access; they are not evidence that the entry skill has been assessed in practice.

Useful NS: add training to the explanation; find the Entry need field; or say where the need came from. Retain the first answer and reply. Judge the two outcome parts separately. No inference about real eligibility or future job success.

Exact evidence: Apprenticeship fact card. Retain chosen profile and sector, four labelled facts, earn-and-learn explanation, one application need and source, actual access, answer prompts, first response, NS and reply. Secure explanation includes paid work plus training; secure application need comes from the selected card. Record partial evidence honestly. A no-response or pass is unobserved.

Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank fields for either profile. Save with the usual routine, lesson code and work reference; show privately. Scribe exact words or selections, read back and allow correction. Book or usual aid is valid. No online form is sent and no application is made.

E means actual evidence banked; R follows Voice, Audience, one NS and the learner’s reply. Add to Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

Trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass, supported pause/return and usual aids remain available. No real grades, personal job history or family finances requested. Listen calmly, avoid probing and secrecy promises and follow normal procedures. Keep concerns outside public evidence.
